entries.clue: Finding age not bad, racing away (6,6)

indicators.note: racing away: the letters run off and rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone discovers that getting older isn't so bad once they've given up racing.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'bad' hides that 'not bad, racing' is one run of fodder; 'Finding age' is a description of what the technique does.
annotation.definitionFit: Carbon dating is the method scientists use to find the age of organic remains.

entries.clue: Cool-headed learner in river (4)

indicators.note: the learner sits in the river

blocks.note: the Cam, the river through Cambridge
L = learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A student keeps their composure while swimming in a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river that runs through Cambridge, a favourite crossword river.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone calm keeps their head under pressure.

entries.clue: Not beginning with child on the throne (7)

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: regnant means reigning

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A queen who is not yet expecting an heir sits on her throne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With child' reads as company for the monarch, but it is the old phrase for pregnant; behead PREGNANT.
annotation.definitionFit: Regnant describes a ruler who is currently reigning, as in queen regnant.

entries.clue: Drunk cooked without top on (5)

indicators.note: a down answer's top is its first letter, here taken off

annotation.surface: Someone has been drinking and has cooked dinner without bothering to put a shirt on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well oiled' is informal British for drunk; the solver must behead BOILED.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British sense, from the phrase 'well oiled', meaning lubricated with drink.

entries.clue: Daughter never relocated to US city (6)

indicators.note: the letters of NEVER are moved to new places

annotation.surface: A daughter who has never moved house finally relocates to an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Never relocated' reads as someone who stayed put, which is exactly the misdirection; it is an instruction to rearrange NEVER.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the capital of Colorado is one of many US cities.

entries.clue: Portion of a trench unearthed (7)

indicators.note: dug up, so the letters are turned over into a new order

annotation.surface: Archaeologists dig out part of a trench.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a dig, and 'unearthed' fits it so well that it hides its job of stirring the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice, especially of money or shares.

entries.clue: In Ghana a fine canteen service (inits) (5)

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A traveller praises the service at a canteen in Ghana.
annotation.walkthrough: The NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) runs canteens and shops for the British armed forces; '(inits)' tells you the answer is a set of initials.
annotation.definitionFit: The NAAFI is the organisation that provides canteens for British servicemen and women.

entries.clue: Disreputable to be far back from angle (7)

indicators.note: 'Back' means in reverse, so far is read from its end to its start.

blocks.note: to angle is to fish with a rod; 'from' puts it after

annotation.surface: A shady character keeps well back from an awkward angle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Angle' looks like geometry but is the verb meaning to fish with rod and line.
annotation.definitionFit: Raffish means rakish and a little disreputable, often in an attractive way.

entries.clue: Member, Capone, is lawful (5)

blocks.note: a limb is a member of the body

annotation.surface: A gang member insists that Al Capone is on the right side of the law.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that the notorious gangster Capone is called lawful; 'Member' means a limb, not a mobster.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal and lawful both mean permitted by law.

entries.clue: Returning once more with artist to river (7)

indicators.note: coming back, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician, a crossword artist

annotation.surface: A painter goes back to a river again to paint it.
annotation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, the standard crossword artist; the Niagara river runs between Lakes Erie and Ontario.
annotation.definitionFit: The Niagara is the river that carries the famous falls.

entries.clue: Worried a French kid, he's given tissue (12)

indicators.note: worried in the sense of worked at and pulled about, so the letters are disturbed

annotation.surface: A tearful French child is handed a tissue.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma and the ''s' make 'he' look like the subject of the sentence, but it joins the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A handkerchief is a square of cloth, or loosely a tissue, for wiping the nose or eyes.

entries.clue: Racking up high-speed gnomes (7)

definitions.note: racking is a mass noun for a set of shelves; the answer is the plural noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: HS = high-speed, as in the British HS2 rail line
gnomes and elves are both little folk of folklore

annotation.surface: Someone clocks up great speed chasing garden gnomes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racking up' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Racking' is the definition and 'up' turns the abbreviation round, as a down answer is read from the bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Racking is the trade word for a framework of shelves, as in warehouse or bike racking.

entries.clue: Playful tot in centre of jacuzzi (3,3)

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of tot
the rearranged tot goes inside the centre

annotation.surface: A child splashes about in the middle of a jacuzzi.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Centre' tempts you to take the middle letters of jacuzzi, but here it is a synonym, and jacuzzi is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Jacuzzi is a brand name that has become a general word for a hot tub.

entries.clue: Left on plate? You, say! Tidy up! (7)

indicators.note: spoken, you sounds like the letter U

blocks.note: to neaten is to tidy up

annotation.surface: A parent scolds a child who has left food on the plate and a mess to tidy.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Left on plate' is an example rather than a dictionary definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: food still on the plate is one thing that has not been eaten.

entries.clue: One in class is a brilliant person (6)

indicators.note: one is placed in the class

blocks.note: a genus is a class in biology

annotation.surface: The top pupil in the class is praised as brilliant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Class' is a biological rank, not a school form.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names the exceptionally gifted person as well as the gift itself.

entries.clue: Frozen little rabbit gets a sweet treat (4,3)

blocks.note: bun, short for bunny, a child's word for a rabbit

annotation.surface: A cold little bunny is rewarded with a treat.
annotation.walkthrough: An iced bun is a sweet bread roll topped with sugar icing, a British bakery staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the sugar-topped British bakery roll is one kind of sweet treat.

entries.clue: Sound animal with a frog in its throat? (6)

definitions.text: with a frog in its throat?

indicators.note: the answer is heard as the word for the animal

blocks.note: the spoken name of a farm animal you can ride, spelt as a different word

annotation.surface: A picture of a creature with a frog stuck in its throat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A frog in the throat' is the idiom for a croaky voice; 'Sound' looks like an adjective (healthy) but is the instruction to hear the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone with a frog in their throat has a rough, croaky voice: the idiom and the answer describe the same thing.

entries.clue: Dear sir, L (6-6)

blocks.note: the words that open a formal letter
L is the opening letter of the word LETTER

annotation.surface: The start of a formal letter, as if someone began writing and stopped after one letter.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is really a knife for slitting envelopes, but neither definition means that: both are playful readings of 'letter opener'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Dear sir' is what opens a letter, and L is what opens the word 'letter'.

entries.clue: City tour possibly includes river (5)

indicators.note: tour is only one possible order of these letters
the rearranged tour takes R inside

annotation.surface: A city sightseeing tour takes in a river cruise.
annotation.walkthrough: TRURO is the cathedral city of Cornwall, in south-west England.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the cathedral city of Cornwall is one example of a city.

entries.clue: Precise former deed (5)

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

annotation.surface: A lawyer pins down the precise wording of an old deed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deed' suggests a legal document but just means an act.
annotation.definitionFit: Exact and precise both mean accurate in every detail.

entries.clue: Teacher has time in prison (4)

indicators.note: the teacher holds time inside

blocks.note: pupils in British schools call a male teacher 'sir'

annotation.surface: A teacher is doing time behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is old British slang for prison; 'has time' looks like idle leisure but means T goes inside SIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, as in 'doing time in stir'.

entries.clue: Hotline around the globe? (7)

blocks.note: the surface reads an emergency telephone link; the setter means a line that is hot
the surface reads worldwide reach; the setter means a line circling the Earth itself

annotation.surface: A telephone hotline that connects the whole world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotline' suggests an emergency phone link; split it into hot line, and the globe is the Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: The equator is the imaginary line around the Earth's middle, where the climate is hottest.

entries.clue: Superior, British in flying boat (5)

indicators.note: 'In' says one thing sits inside another, so British is placed within the rearranged boat.
the letters of boat fly about into a new order

annotation.surface: A top-quality British flying boat, like the old seaplanes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying boat' is a real kind of seaplane, which hides the anagram; 'Superior' is a noun, the head of a religious house.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword favourite: 'Superior' as a noun is the head of a religious house, which for a community of monks is this title.

entries.clue: Singer with bar and note to hear (7-5)

indicators.note: the note's name is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: a counter is a bar in a shop or pub
a tenner is a ten-pound note

annotation.surface: A singer takes a bar stool and a banknote to hear a performance.
annotation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note; 'note' looks musical, which fits a singer, but it is money.
annotation.definitionFit: A countertenor is a male singer with a voice above tenor.
